frontier.hypothesis: The last 2 instructions are one dead reg-reg copy per scan loop, emitted by a GCC pass rather than written in C, and the pass can be named from the dumps already on disk.
frontier.mechanism: Target routes the loop base's addend through `addu a3,a0,zero` - a copy of the pre-guard pointer that is read once by the next `addu a0,a1,a3` and never again, in BOTH preheaders. C-level copies are closed by name (cse.c / combine.c, s6), and in our build the addend dies at the base's own insn (REG_DEAD reg/v77 on insn 158 of s7/O/ings_pp.c.combine), which is precisely why no copy is needed. So the question is which pass emits a redundant move INTO a loop preheader, and what source shape stops the addend dying at the base insn.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c `move_movables` (the `m->move_insn` path emits `(set new old)` at the loop start when a movable's source register may be modified) and local-alloc.c `block_alloc`/`combine_regs` (the tie-the-output-to-a-dying-input path) against the dumps already in tmp/grind/func_80017848/s7/O/ - ings_pp.c.loop, .lreg, .greg. Then build the C shape those passes require and score it with s7/score.sh. Do NOT re-propose a source-level copy statement (s6 pass-level kill) and do NOT re-open base placement, an explicit shift local, explicit links locals, or swapped guard/base roles (all killed this session).

frontier.hypothesis: The register-naming residual (ours slots=a2 / links=a1 vs target slots=v1 / links=a2) is downstream of frontier item 1 and should not be attacked separately first.
frontier.mechanism: Ours keeps `slots` live across both scan loops because the loop bases consume it; target's top-guard slots read dies after the two `>=0` guards and each preheader instead copies the fresh pre-guard pointer. If the copy in frontier item 1 is solved by giving the base's addend its own short live range, `slots` stops being live across the loops and the naming should follow for free.
frontier.next_probe: After ANY movement on frontier item 1, re-diff with s7/dis2.sh and check whether the slots/links register assignment collapsed to target's without further work. Only if it did not should the allocator's preference records in s7/O/ings_pp.c.greg be read as their own mechanism.

frontier.hypothesis: Every remaining banked spelling conclusion from s3/s4/s5/s6 is chassis-relative to a chassis that has now changed TWICE, and must be re-run before it is spent.
frontier.mechanism: s6 retired the s3/s4/s5 chassis as semantically divergent; s7 then found s6's own D/G verdict inverted in sign on the corrected chassis (the fold-defeat lever went from -1 to +3). What survives untouched is only the pass-level kills (H-s6-2, H-s6-3, H-s7-3..H-s7-6), because they are RTL facts rather than score comparisons.
frontier.next_probe: Before spending any banked spelling conclusion, re-run it as a matched pair against the s7 candidate with s7/score.sh (one blocking call scores a whole list of bodies from a clean tree). Do not re-open a broad preheader sweep - targeted re-validation only.
